title: Allo pricing, features, & limitations: everything to know in 2026
summary: Allo pricing: Plans, features, and limitations
body_markdown:
Allo’s website promotes its ability to handle more phone calls, with the intent of replacing legacy software. While it offers many common capabilities familiar to contact centers around the world, it misses the mark for growing teams.


In this guide, we’ll cover Allo pricing for businesses, its features, limitations, and any additional fees you may have to pay. We’ll also share an


[alternative to Allo](https://www.quo.com/blog/allo-alternatives/) that can be a better fit for teams.


##

The lowest plan requires you to pay for the whole year up front. The Solo plan is pretty bare bones compared to the more expensive plans beyond basic calling and messaging. The high-tier plans offer more contact center-specific features along with AI agents.


Let’s take a closer look at each plan.


### **Solo Plan**


**Pricing:** $120 per user per year. Annual only, no month-to-month.


**Best for:** Freelancers and solopreneurs


**Free trial:** No


The Solo plan allows for unlimited national calling and inbound messages. However, you can’t send any outbound messages and you only have one phone number and one user for the entire account. Since it’s meant for solo operators, it doesn’t have a shared inbox or other team-specific features. A lot of Allo’s more powerful AI features are also missing. Solo operators only get access to the AI transcript and[call summary](https://www.quo.com/features/call-summary) features, which cover only 30 days of call history.


Here’s what you do get:


- One business number, free porting
- Mobile, desktop, and web apps
- Picture-in-picture call window
- Pay-as-you-go international calling
- IVR and[call routing](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing)
- Internal CRM


Keep in mind, the Solo plan is listed as “Coming Soon” on the website, so it might not be available to most customers right now.


### **Business Plan**


**Pricing:** $45 per user per month. $32 if paid annually.


**Best for:** Mid-sized sales and support teams


**Free trial:** Seven days


The Business plan includes one phone number per user. The plan has team-specific features, including:


- Shared inbox
- Shared notes
- Zapier and Make integrations
- [Call analytics](https://www.quo.com/blog/call-analytics)
- Unlimited call history for summaries and transcripts
- AI call tags
- Click-to-call extension


However, it **** lacks the advanced AI features of the Ultra plan. Power dialing is a paid upgrade.


### **Ultra Plan**


**Pricing:** $120 per user per month. $100 if paid annually.


**Best for:** Large teams and call centers


**Free trial:** Contact sales


Beyond the custom analytics dashboard and higher levels of support, the Ultra plan’s value mostly comes from Allo’s AI agents. Here are the specifics:


- AI SDR
- AI Sales Coach
- AI Data Analyst
- AI Lead Qualifier
- Create your own agent


All these agents are marked as “Beta” in the pricing sheet, which implies they’re still in development and may not perform as advertised.


##


Additional costs that come with using Allo


Here are some other factors that you should know about before signing up with Allo:


- **Shared inbox.** The base plan doesn’t have a shared inbox. It’s only for Business plan users and above.
- **SMS.** You can’t send outbound messages from the base Allo plan. You need to upgrade to Business plan, and even when you do, unlimited SMS is only included in the US plan. Other locations are pay-as-you-go.
- **Power dialer.** Power dialers are only available as a paid upgrade to Business and Ultra users for $50 per month. Solo users don’t get access at all.
- **AI features.** Solo gets basic AI features like call summary and transcription. However, these are only available for calls within the last 30 days unless you upgrade. AI receptionists are a paid upgrade at $32 per month. More advanced AI-powered workflows and agents are only available on the higher tiers.
- **Advanced onboarding.** Only Ultra users and Business accounts with more than five users can access advanced onboarding and get assigned a dedicated account manager.

##


Pros and cons of Allo pricing plans


Allo is a good option for mid-sized and enterprise-level companies that want to streamline operations. Smaller teams with a limited budget may need to look elsewhere, especially if they need to collaborate closely.


**Pros**


- **Built for outbound sales.** Allo provides features that support sales outreach, including AI-driven outbound SMS and power dialing.


- **International numbers.** Allo offers phone numbers in 120+ countries. ****


- **Native CRM sync.** Calls and transcripts sync with the CRM as soon as a call ends, no manual entry required.


**Cons**


- **Beta features.** The Ultra plan costs at least $100 per user per month, yet most AI agents in that tier are still in beta and not fully developed.


- **Locked in for a year.** The Solo plan requires a one-year commitment if you sign up, with no free trial period.


- **Costly SMS.** You need the Business plan to send any outbound SMS, and it’s only free for US numbers. For other locations, they give you $5 of credit per seat per month and then it’s pay-as-you-go.


- **Limited base plan.** No outbound SMS. Important collaboration features, like shared inboxes and shared notes, are locked behind higher tiers.

##


FAQs


**Which Allo plans have a free trial?**


Only the Business plan has a seven-day free trial. Free trials aren’t available for the Solo or Ultra plans.


**How long is Allo’s free trial?**


Allo offers a seven-day free trial for Business plans only.


**Does Allo charge per minute for calls?**


Users can make unlimited local calls. However, international calls are charged per-minute based on the destination and whether it’s a mobile or landline.


**How much does Allo cost compared to other alternatives?**


Allo’s prices start at $120 a year for the Solo plan. There’s also no free trial for the Solo plan. That means you won’t be able to try it out and you’re locked in for at least one year. Quo’s Starter plan is $19 per user per month if you pay month to month. To save more, you can pay annually, which is $15 per user per month.


**Do I have to pay an entire year for the Solo plan?**


Yes. There’s no month-to-month option for Solo plan users.


**Which Allo features are currently in beta?**


Most of Allo’s advanced AI agent types are currently in beta, including AI SDR, AI Sales Coach, and AI Data Analyst. The “Create Your Own Agent” feature is also in beta.


**What kind of support does Allo provide?**


Solo plans have access to email support only. Business accounts get email and live chat support, and accounts with more than five users have a dedicated account manager and custom onboarding. Ultra accounts get all the support options from the previous plans, plus Slack support, an SLA, and more granular admin controls.
